The '''Czech football champions''' indicates all past winners of the top-tier [[Association football|football]] leagues in which clubs from [[Czech Republic]] were inserted in.  It includes the [[Czechoslovak First League]] and current [[Czech First League]].

==History==
Bohemia was an early adopter of football.<ref name="Smolík">{{cite web|url=http://www.uff.br/esportesociedade/pdf/es303.pdf|title=Football fan culture in the Czech Republic : Development, problems, causes|first=Josef|last=Smolík|website=Uff.br|accessdate=15 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020230110/http://www.uff.br/esportesociedade/pdf/es303.pdf|archive-date=20 October 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aH1PpJFygvsC&dq=football+in+czechoslovakia&pg=PA233|title=Football: The First Hundred Years: The Untold Story|first=Adrian|last=Harvey|date=13 May 2013|publisher=Routledge|isbn=9781134269129|accessdate=14 October 2017|via=Google Books}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.radio.cz/en/section/czech-history/tribute-to-czech-football-legend-josef-masopust-1931-2015|title=Tribute to Czech football legend Josef Masopust (1931 – 2015)|first=Chris|last=Johnstone|website=Radio.cz|date=29 June 2015|accessdate=14 October 2017}}</ref> Football originated in Bohemia in early 1890s, when two of the most famous clubs, [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta]] and [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia]], were founded. They met for the first time, for a rivalry later to become known as the [[Prague derby]], in March 1896.<ref name="Smolík"/>

The first Bohemian championship (1896) was won by ČFK Kickers Prague (spring). [[DFC Prag|Deutscher Fußball-Club Prag]] won the championship in autumn of the same year. In 1897 Slavia were victorious for a number of years until, in 1902, the championship was won by [[ČAFC Prague|ČAFC Vinohrady]]. The [[Czechoslovak First League]] was the highest football league in Czechoslovakia from 1925 to 1993.
